Subject: Lumina - Dedicated SKU scenario proposal & follow-ups

Hi Alex — thanks again for the 30m call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size a dedicated proposal that matches Lumina's constraints.

TL;DR:
- Lumina is leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) because of data residency and predictable throughput needs, but may require Private/VPC later for PHI-specific workflows.
- You mentioned a peak traffic profile and token mix below — please confirm.
- Attached: a short sizing workbook (lumina-dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx) to fill with examples/test payloads.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant + patient messaging inference. No model training on our side, inference-only.
- Latency objective: p95 <= 200ms for short prompts; some long inference paths allowed up to 800ms p95 (non-critical).
- Target concurrent sessions (observed peak day): ~60 concurrent requests, with spikes to ~90 for short-burst campaigns.
- TPS profile: ~40 TPS steady-state, peak up to 80 TPS for short windows (1–5 min).
- Token mix: ~80% short (average 35 tokens), ~20% long (average 380 tokens). Typical avg tokens per request ~80.
- Security: PHI handling for some endpoints — you noted that initial rollout may live in Dedicated in our hosted VPC but Private/VPC-on-prem is possible for full PHI scope.

Asks / next steps for you:
1) Can you confirm the above numbers (concurrency, TPS, token averages) and share an anonymized example payload (or avg tokens per request by endpoint)?
2) Any hard constraints on GPU vendor? You said you were evaluating A10G vs A100 for cost/perf tradeoffs — if you have procurement constraints please flag.
3) Are lifecycle requirements (data retention, log access, audit windows) in the attached workbook OK to fill out?

What we'll do next internally:
- Ben and Vivek will size two SKU scenarios: a cost-optimized A10G-based reserved pool and a performance A100-backed pool, with estimated latency, token cost/1M, and lead times.
- We'll include a canary rollout plan (gradual traffic ramp + automatic fallback to hosted variants).

I left the recording in the Drive link and attached the workbook. If this summary looks right, a quick confirm from you on numbers and one sample payload will let us send back the SKU options by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,

Hi Naomi — thanks for the notes and the workbook. Confirming the key numbers and answering your asks below.

Confirmations:
- Concurrency: steady ~50 concurrent, but realistic peak windows hit ~85 for short bursts (marketing-driven messages).
- TPS: steady 35–45 TPS, peak ~80 TPS for 2–7 minute windows.
- Token mix: agree with your breakout. Our production logs show ~78% requests < 60 tokens, ~17% in 60–400, ~5% >400. Avg tokens/request across endpoints ~72.

GPU preference and constraints:
- No strict vendor lock, but procurement prefers lower-cost options where SLA still met. A10G would be attractive if it meets latency targets for short prompts. We know A100 gives headroom but has longer lead times and higher cost.

Security / deployment notes:
- We handle PHI in a subset of features. Short-term: Dedicated in a Redwood-managed VPC with strict IAM and encrypted at-rest will probably suffice. Long-term: we will likely need a Private VPC or on-prem option for full PHI compliance across all endpoints.

I'll attach an anonymized sample payload and a short CSV with token stats per endpoint to the workbook by EOD.

One more ask: what are expected cold-start characteristics for new model variants on Dedicated capacity? Some of our endpoints will experiment with larger context windows from time to time.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll fill the workbook and send it back.

— Alex

Thanks Naomi — drafting now. Initial high-level sizing notes (very rough, will refine after Vivek runs perf sim):

1) Cost-optimized (A10G pool) - baseline for steady-state:
- Suggested pool: 12 x A10G (reserved).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~35–45 TPS for our tuned Llama-2-Chat-like variant with batching and KV caching.
- Concurrency headroom at 12 GPUs (with continuous batching): ~70 concurrent short requests; bursts to ~100 may introduce queuing or higher p95.
- Estimated token cost: ~ $X per 1M tokens (will provide a matrix after perf sims).
- Provisioning/lead time: typically 2–3 weeks for reserved capacity.

2) Performance (A100 pool) - headroom + experimentation:
- Suggested pool: 6 x A100 (reserve) + 4 x A10G burst capacity (optional).
- Expected throughput: A100s give ~2–3x per-device throughput for long-context workloads; p95 short should be comfortably below 200ms.
- Concurrency headroom: comfortably handles 100+ concurrent short requests with lower queuing.
- Estimated token cost: higher vs A10G but better latency profile; will provide delta table.
- Provisioning/lead time: A100 lead time 3–6 weeks.

Operational notes / asks for Alex:
- Please share the anonymized payload and token CSV so Vivek can run local perf sim and provide calibrated numbers (p95 expectations by prompt length).
- Recommend a small synthetic perf run: 10k requests with your token mix to validate batching behavior; we can run on our test pool and share traces.
- For PHI-sensitive endpoints, we’ll include a Private/VPC cost add-on in the proposal. The workbook schema will capture retention and audit needs.

Next: Vivek will send perf sim outputs and we’ll return a short two-slide cost/latency comparison.

—Ben
